biblio.label: JP S6165742 A
biblio.title: permanent magnet chuck
biblio.assignee: KANETSUU KOGYO KK, Kanetsu Kogyo KK
biblio.abstract: (57) [Summary] This bulletin contains application data before electronic filing, so abstract data is not recorded.

summary: This document discloses a permanent magnet chuck that effectively magnetizes the whole magnetic zone of a surface plate and improves its magnetic attractive force by switching the surface plate between magnetized and non-magnetized conditions.

rows.label: claim 1[b]
rows.claim_text: a magnet which is arranged in the housing and which is displaceable along a displacement direction between a gripping position for gripping the ferromagnetic workpiece and a release position for releasing the ferromagnetic workpiece
rows.claim_paraphrase: a magnet which is arranged in the housing and which is displaceable along a displacement direction between a gripping position for gripping the ferromagnetic workpiece and a …
rows.quote: a permanent magnet able to move in the vertical direction between a bottom plate and the surface plate.
rows.note: This passage describes a permanent magnet that moves in the vertical direction between a bottom plate and a surface plate, which corresponds to a magnet displaceable along a displacement direction between a gripping and release position.
rows.disclosure: The reference discloses a permanent magnet able to move in the vertical direction between a bottom plate and the surface plate, which corresponds to a magnet displaceable along a displacement direction between a gripping and release position.

rows.label: claim 1[c]
rows.claim_text: a number of pole shoes attached to the housing, wherein each pole shoe has a workpiece contact surface and is designed to guide a magnetic field portion of the magnet to the workpiece contact surface
rows.claim_paraphrase: a number of pole shoes attached to the housing, wherein each pole shoe has a workpiece contact surface and is designed to guide a magnetic field portion of the magnet to the …
rows.quote: a magnetic pole part 14, brought into contact with a yoke 26, and each magnetic zone 14a of a surface plate, brought into contact with a yoke upper magnetic part 24b, are alternately magnetized in a different magnetic pole placing
rows.note: The reference discloses magnetic pole parts (pole shoes) and a surface plate (workpiece contact surface) that guide magnetic flux.
rows.disclosure: The reference discloses a magnetic pole part 14 brought into contact with a yoke 26, and each magnetic zone 14a of a surface plate, brought into contact with a yoke upper magnetic part 24b, which are alternately magnetized and guide magnetic flux.

rows.label: claim 2[b]
rows.claim_text: the displacement direction is aligned parallel to the longitudinal axis of the housing
rows.claim_paraphrase: the displacement direction is aligned parallel to the longitudinal axis of the housing
rows.quote: The permanent magnets 20 are rigidly supported by each frame 34 so as to be aligned in the same magnetization direction, and as shown in FIG. 26 , that is, the magnetic a1 of the face plate 16? The magnetization
rows.note: The reference describes the movement of permanent magnets in a vertical direction, which could be considered a displacement direction.
rows.disclosure: The reference discloses permanent magnets 20 that are rigidly supported by each frame 34 so as to be aligned in the same magnetization direction, and move in the vertical direction.

rows.label: claim 3[a]
rows.claim_text: The magnetic gripper according to claim 1, wherein each pole shoe has an active structure for directing the magnetic field portion
rows.claim_paraphrase: The magnetic gripper according to claim 1, wherein each pole shoe has an active structure for directing the magnetic field portion
rows.quote: In the upper position of a frame structure 34 supporting a magnet 20, a magnetic pole part 14, brought into contact with a yoke 26, and each magnetic zone 14a of a surface plate, brought into contact with a yoke
rows.note: The reference describes magnetic pole parts and yokes that guide magnetic flux to the surface plate, which can be interpreted as directing the magnetic field.
rows.disclosure: The reference discloses a magnetic pole part 14 brought into contact with a yoke 26, and each magnetic zone 14a of a surface plate, brought into contact with a yoke, which direct the magnetic field.

rows.label: claim 6[c]
rows.claim_text: the active structure has a recess between the first projection and the second projection
rows.claim_paraphrase: the active structure has a recess between the first projection and the second projection
rows.quote: A recess 32 for the permanent magnet 20 is defined between the adjacent magnetic yokes 24 and 26 by spacers 28 and 30 in which an upper spacer 28 and a lower spacer 30 made of a non-magnetic material are
rows.note: The reference discloses a recess between adjacent magnetic yokes, which could be considered an active structure.
rows.disclosure: The reference discloses a recess 32 for the permanent magnet 20 defined between the adjacent magnetic yokes 24 and 26 by spacers 28 and 30.

rows.label: claim 8[b]
rows.claim_text: the magnet is arranged in the housing such that, in the gripping position, the first pole shoe acts as a north pole and the second pole shoe acts as a south pole
rows.claim_paraphrase: the magnet is arranged in the housing such that, in the gripping position, the first pole shoe acts as a north pole and the second pole shoe acts as a south pole
rows.quote: are alternately magnetized in a different magnetic pole placing the surface plate 16 in a magnetized condition because a magnetic pole surface adapted to a yoke 24 of each permanent magnet 20 is brought into contact with only the upper
rows.note: The reference states that magnetic pole parts are alternately magnetized in a different magnetic pole, which implies north and south poles.
rows.disclosure: The reference discloses that magnetic pole parts are alternately magnetized in a different magnetic pole, placing the surface plate 16 in a magnetized condition because a magnetic pole surface adapted to a yoke 24 of each permanent magnet 20 is brought into contact with only the upper part.

rows.label: claim 14[d]
rows.claim_text: wherein, in a release state, the magnet is in the release position and the ferromagnetic workpiece is not pressed, by means of a magnetic force, against each workpiece contact surface
rows.claim_paraphrase: wherein, in a release state, the magnet is in the release position and the ferromagnetic workpiece is not pressed, by means of a magnetic force, against each workpiece contact …
rows.quote: Next in the bottom position of the frame structure 34, the surface plate 16 is placed in a non-magnetized condition by forming closed loop magnetic flux via the yoke 26, yoke bottom magnetic part 24C and a bottom plate 18
rows.note: This passage describes the surface plate being in a non-magnetized condition when the magnet is in the bottom position, meaning a workpiece would not be pressed by magnetic force, which corresponds to a release state.
rows.disclosure: The reference discloses that in the bottom position of the frame structure 34, the surface plate 16 is placed in a non-magnetized condition by forming closed loop magnetic flux via the yoke 26, yoke bottom magnetic part 24C and a bottom plate 18, meaning the ferromagnetic workpiece is not pressed by magnetic force.

rows.claim_text: The magnetic gripper according to claim 1, wherein the receptacle is in the form of a groove

rows.note: The reference discloses a 'recess' for the permanent magnet, which could be considered a type of receptacle.
rows.disclosure: The reference discloses a recess 32 for the permanent magnet 20 defined between the adjacent magnetic yokes 24 and 26.
